drivingQuestion: What do the inclusive terms of the mishna add?
outcomeNote: Each inclusive clause assigned a case

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ ״הַכֹּל מַעֲלִין״ לְאֵתוֹיֵי מַאי? לְאֵתוֹיֵי עֲבָדִים.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» The mishna stated: «All» can force the members of their family «to ascend.» The Gemara asks: This inclusive phrase serves «to include what» case? The Gemara answers: It comes «to include slaves,» i.e., Hebrew slaves as well may be coerced to immigrate to Eretz Yisrael with their master’s family against their will.

segments.he: וּלְמַאן דְּתָנֵי עֲבָדִים בְּהֶדְיָא, לְאֵתוֹיֵי מַאי? לְאֵתוֹיֵי מִנָּוֶה הַיָּפֶה לְנָוֶה הָרַע(ה).
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «And according to the one» whose text of the mishna «expressly teaches» the case of «slaves,» this phrase comes «to include what» case? As stated later in the Gemara, there are some editions of the mishna that state that this halakha applies equally to men, women, and slaves. The Gemara answers: It comes «to include» one who moves «from a pleasant residence to a noxious residence,» i.e., one may coerce his family to ascend to Eretz Yisrael even from a good residence abroad to an inferior one in Eretz Yisrael.

segments.he: ״וְאֵין הַכֹּל מוֹצִיאִין״ לְאֵתוֹיֵי מַאי? לְאֵתוֹיֵי עֶבֶד שֶׁבָּרַח מֵחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ לָאָרֶץ, דְּאָמְרִינַן לֵיהּ: זַבְּנֵיהּ הָכָא וְזִיל, מִשּׁוּם יְשִׁיבַת אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל.
segments.en: § The mishna further taught: «But all may not remove» others. Once again the Gemara asks: This phrase comes «to include what» case? The Gemara answers: It comes «to include a» Canaanite «slave who ran away» from his master and came «from outside Eretz» Yisrael «to Eretz» Yisrael, «as we say to» the master: «Sell» your slave «here,» in Eretz Yisrael, «and» then you may «go» and return abroad, but you may not take the slave abroad with you, «due to» the mitzva of «settling Eretz Yisrael.»

segments.he: ״הַכֹּל מַעֲלִין לִירוּשָׁלַיִם״ לְאֵתוֹיֵי מַאי? לְאֵתוֹיֵי מִנָּוֶה הַיָּפֶה לְנָוֶה הָרַע(ה).
segments.en: § The mishna taught: «All» may force others «to ascend to Jerusalem.» The Gemara asks once again: This phrase comes «to include what» case? The Gemara answers: It comes «to include» a move «from a pleasant residence» elsewhere in Eretz Yisrael «to a noxious residence» in Jerusalem.

segments.he: ״וְאֵין הַכֹּל מוֹצִיאִין״ לְאֵתוֹיֵי מַאי? לְאֵתוֹיֵי אֲפִילּוּ מִנָּוֶה הָרַע(ה) לְנָוֶה הַיָּפֶה. וְאַיְּידֵי דִּתְנָא רֵישָׁא ״אֵין מוֹצִיאִין״, תְּנָא סֵיפָא נָמֵי ״אֵין מוֹצִיאִין״.
segments.en: § The mishna taught: «And all may not remove» them from Jerusalem. The Gemara asks: This phrase comes «to include what» case? The Gemara answers: It comes «to include even» a move «from a noxious residence to a pleasant residence.» The Gemara adds: «And since» the tanna of the mishna «taught: But one may not remove, in the first clause, he also taught: But one may not remove, in the latter clause,» despite the fact that this halakha could have been inferred from the first clause.
